clue.text: Getting on so well, as we all know

definitions.meaning: people who get on brilliantly are said to get on like a house on fire, or in this idiom, splendidly
a sentence adverb meaning notoriously, as is common knowledge

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: getting on extremely well together, and an ironic aside meaning as is widely known.

clue.text: Did wrong to impound vehicle, producing official documentation

indicators.note: to impound is to shut something in, so one piece goes inside the other
done wrong, the letters of the word did are put in a different order

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone who did wrong has their vehicle impounded and must show their papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did' reads as the past of do in the surface, but its three letters are anagram fodder; 'to impound' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An identity card is a piece of official documentation proving who you are.

clue.text: Commonly, school jumper needs treating initially in starch

indicators.note: common speech drops its aitches, so the initial H of the school's name goes

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school
a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A schoolboy athlete needs some starch treatment, in a confusing culinary sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' drops the H from HARROW to give ARROW, the way a Cockney would say it. 'Jumper' looks like a sweater but is the kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowroot is a starch extracted from the rhizomes of a tropical plant, used to thicken sauces.

clue.text: Day's wet, filling this?

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A rainy day fills the gutter outlet to overflowing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: on a wet day, rainwater fills the outlet the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain is the channel or pipe that rainwater on a wet day runs into and fills.

clue.text: Shabby appearance remarked

indicators.note: something remarked is spoken, so the word is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: mien is a person's bearing or appearance

explanation.surface: Someone comments that a person looks shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can describe something poor and shabby in quality, as in a mean little room.

clue.text: Joint study perhaps that one needs to manoeuvre

parts.note: the elbow is a joint of the arm
a study is an example of a room in a house

explanation.surface: Someone moving furniture into a study finds they need space to turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is space enough to move freely, which is what manoeuvring requires.

clue.text: Sweet to study a female out of tenderness

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: out of means these letters are taken away from the longer word

parts.note: affection is tenderness

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to study a woman simply out of tender feeling, with a sweet on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' looks like 'because of' in the surface, but it signals removing A and F, given by 'a female', from the synonym for tenderness.
explanation.definitionFit: A confection is a sweet, a dish or delicacy made with sugar.

clue.text: Skirt length shortened among set of clothes

indicators.note: among means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: kit is a set of clothes, as in football kit

indicators.note: shortened means the word length is cut to its first letter, the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A skirt has been taken up and packed with other clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilt is a pleated knee-length skirt, traditionally worn by Scottish men.

clue.text: What de Gaulle gave our Common Market application soon

definitions.text: What de Gaulle gave our Common Market application
definitions.meaning: de Gaulle vetoed Britain's 1963 bid to join the EEC, giving it a French refusal, a 'non'
an old word for soon or shortly

explanation.walkthrough: President de Gaulle of France famously said non to Britain joining the European Common Market.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an archaic adverb meaning shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: Killing time

parts.note: read not as idling away hours but as the period when hunting a species is permitted

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase wants to mean passing time idly; instead it is the season when killing game is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the period when game may legally be hunted, so a time for killing.

clue.text: One priestly and laic curiously accepted

parts.note: a canon is a member of the clergy, one who is priestly

indicators.note: curiously signals that the letters of laic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchman and a layman are oddly both welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: Canonical means authorised or generally accepted, as in a canonical text.

clue.text: Boat turned into a national symbol

indicators.note: turned means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed boat, as on the Tyne

explanation.surface: A boat is converted into a monument for the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The leek is the national emblem of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is an emblem of Wales, worn on St David's Day, so a national symbol.

clue.text: Primate's outrageous work rebuffed

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being turned back, so the pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means outrageous
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An archbishop's scandalous composition is rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, but it is the animal; 'rebuffed' turns OTTOP round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The potto is a slow-moving African primate related to the lorises.

clue.text: Such arms carried little at first

indicators.note: at first means this piece comes before the other

parts.note: small means little
bore is the past tense of bear, to carry

explanation.surface: Weapons of this kind were carried by children at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-bore describes firearms with a narrow barrel, such as .22 rifles.

clue.text: German who has lost a few pounds?

definitions.text: who has lost a few pounds?
definitions.meaning: a person on a diet who has shed some weight

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, playful sense: a slimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name typical in Germany, and also one who follows a diet to reduce weight.

clue.text: Having provocative appearance, began scrubbing face

indicators.note: scrubbing the face removes the front, so the first letter goes

parts.note: started up means began

explanation.surface: Someone with a racy look began washing their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrubbing face' takes S off STARTED UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarted up means dressed or made up in a showy, provocative way.

clue.text: Wicked to grab a pound, and extra pounds?

indicators.note: to grab means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: in slang, wicked and fab both mean excellent
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: It is wicked to pocket a pound, and then some more pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Flab is excess body fat, the pounds of weight someone would like to lose.

clue.text: Her termination, late executed, found moving by English

definitions.text: Her termination, late executed, found moving by English

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted into a new order
executed means beheaded, so the first letter of late is lost

explanation.surface: A queen's death by execution is found affecting by English onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' cuts L from LATE, leaving ATE; with TERMINATION and E, 'moving' rearranges them. The whole clue also describes the French queen guillotined in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: The French queen whose life ended under the guillotine is the woman this whole clue describes.

clue.text: Surplus article replaced by nothing out of the ordinary here

indicators.note: replaced by means one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: surplus goods are unwanted
A is the indefinite article
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Extra goods turn up where nothing unusual normally happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwonted means unaccustomed or unusual, so out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Fast companion on the run

definitions.meaning: the word that goes with fast in the phrase fast and ___, playing deceitfully
escaped and at large, free from captivity

explanation.definitionFit: Its partner word in the idiom 'fast and ___', and also free or at large after escaping.

clue.text: Disparage bird no longer on wing regularly

parts.note: the dodo is an extinct bird

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of wing is taken

explanation.surface: Someone belittles a flightless bird that no longer flies.
explanation.definitionFit: To do down is to belittle or speak disparagingly of someone.

clue.text: In car-boot sale unexpectedly I had body-building aid

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters turn up in a surprising order

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: At a car-boot sale someone unexpectedly came across a gym drug.
explanation.walkthrough: A car-boot sale is a British flea market where people sell from their car boots (trunks).
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids are drugs taken to build muscle, a notorious aid to body-building.

clue.text: Dispatching with charge? Very keen to accept soldier raised appeal

indicators.note: to accept means one piece takes the others inside it

parts.note: dying, as in dying to go, means very keen

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a man is a soldier, as in officers and men
it is sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone eager to get a soldier's backing makes an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means read upwards. The question mark warns that the definition is playful: dispatching means destroying, with an explosive charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing something up with an explosive charge is a way of destroying, or dispatching, it.

clue.text: Cussed fag-end brought to life

parts.note: a stub is the end of a cigarette, called a fag in Britain
born means brought into life

explanation.surface: A cigarette butt somehow comes alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cussed means obstinate or perverse, which is what stubborn means.

clue.text: Distributed cards: apt to keep check in short-term memory

indicators.note: to keep means one piece is held inside the other
distributed, like dealt cards, means the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Cards dealt out help you keep track of a check in your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributed' suggests dealing cards but is the anagram signal for both words; 'to keep' places the chess abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratchpad is a temporary store, either a notepad for jottings or fast working memory in computing.

clue.text: The sort to be thrown, given similar parts?

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
cast means thrown

explanation.surface: The kind of thing to be tossed, given parts that match.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is typecast is always given the same kind of role.

clue.text: Hill, not at all steep, made little impression

parts.note: a fell is a hill, especially in the north of England
flat ground is not steep at all

explanation.surface: A hill with no steep slopes was unimpressive.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke or plan that fell flat failed to make the intended impression.

clue.text: German and I are ruined!

parts.note: und is the German for and
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A German cries out that he and I are done for.
explanation.definitionFit: Undone, in older or dramatic usage, means ruined or brought to destruction.

clue.text: City Hall has altered a bit

indicators.note: a bit means only a portion of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A city's town hall has been slightly modified.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital city of Tibet.

clue.text: Living in tower

definitions.meaning: the strongest central tower of a castle

explanation.definitionFit: One's board and subsistence, and also the fortified central stronghold of a castle.
